heading: Theft
text: Section 378. Whoever, intending to take dishonestly any movable property out of the possession of any person without that person's consent, moves that property in order to such taking, is said to commit theft.

heading: Punishment for theft
text: Section 379. Whoever commits theft shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

heading: Persons in charge of closed place to allow search
text: Section 100 sets out safeguards for searches of closed places, including calling independent and respectable inhabitants to witness the search, conducting the search in their presence, preparing a list of things seized and places where found, and obtaining witness signatures on the list.
source: India Code, Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973

heading: Information in cognizable cases
text: Section 154 governs recording of information relating to a cognizable offence. Oral information to the officer in charge shall be reduced to writing, read over and signed; the substance shall be entered in the prescribed book. A free copy shall be given forthwith to the informant, and subsection (3) supplies a remedy for refusal to record.
source: India Code, Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973

heading: Search by police officer
text: Section 165 permits a police officer in charge of a police station or investigating officer to conduct a necessary search within the statutory conditions, requiring recorded reasons and specification, so far as possible, of the thing sought, with the section 100 search safeguards applying so far as may be.
source: India Code, Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973

heading: Procedure when investigation cannot be completed in twenty-four hours
text: Section 167(2) authorises a Magistrate to order detention in such custody as the Magistrate thinks fit for a term not exceeding fifteen days in the whole. Further detention is subject to the section's conditions and total sixty-day or ninety-day limits, as applicable, with the statutory default-bail consequence on expiry when the accused is prepared to furnish bail.
source: India Code, Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973

heading: Special provisions as to evidence relating to electronic record
text: Section 65A. The contents of electronic records may be proved in accordance with section 65B.

heading: Admissibility of electronic records
text: Section 65B treats qualifying computer output as a document and permits its admission without production of the original when the statutory conditions are met. Those conditions concern regular use, regular feeding of information, proper operation, and faithful reproduction or derivation. Subsection (4) requires the prescribed certificate identifying the record, describing production, giving device particulars, addressing the statutory conditions, and signed by a person occupying a responsible official position.
